meta.title: Permission Gate
meta.description: Deterministic-first, fail-closed permission gate for DeepSeek Harness: P0 hard-deny → P1 session grant → P2 static rules → P3 LLM classifier → P4 ask, with command whitelist and blacklist.

en.card.allowlistHint: Patterns in the allow section allow directly; add or remove entries one by one, written to the rulesFile and reloaded live.
en.card.allowlistPlaceholder: New command pattern, e.g. npm test*
en.card.allowlistPresetNote: The preset-whitelist equivalent is the trustAutoAllow strategy (safe in-scope ops auto-allow), enabled in the strategies section above; this list mirrors your rulesFile allow section and legitimately starts empty.
en.card.askHint: The mechanical screen still filters and lists its doubts, but the ask stays with a person and no grader is called at all — the shape for runs with no reviewer LLM connected, or where the tokens are not worth spending.
en.card.credentialPathsHint: Secret files the built-in list does not know. Entries are path globs: a double star crosses directories, a single star and a question mark stay inside one segment; without a wildcard it matches a whole path fragment (token will not hit ambient.txt); a leading ~/ expands to your home; a relative pattern also matches at any depth (secrets/*.env covers a/b/secrets/prod.env). A hit is held to the same standard as .ssh: reading it outside the workspace is hard-denied, mutating it with a file tool is hard-denied — that tier cannot be appealed or talked past by the reviewer, so declare only paths you truly need protected.
en.card.denyKeywordsExtra: Appended blacklist keywords (never replaces the preset)
en.card.denyKeywordsExtraHint: A deterministic block on words of your own — a revoke/wipe subcommand of a company CLI, a token prefix you issue. This list only ever appends: whatever the blacklist above holds (preset or your own replacement), these words are merged in.
en.card.denylistEmpty: Blacklist empty (no call is vetoed by the keyword layer)
en.card.denylistHint: A call whose text contains a keyword (case-insensitive substring) is denied outright, before whitelist / grants / LLM. The preset list is inherited from dsh-approval-gate and active from install; edit freely — empty or cleared falls back to the preset (one-click restore available), so the blacklist never silently turns off.
en.card.description: Independent approval tier, parallel to read-only / full-access / whitelist, shown as 自动审查 in the session permission picker. The front-end exposes a single switch; the four backend approval strategies are combinable via this panel and still fail-closed against P0 hard-deny.
en.card.dryRunEmpty: Nothing tested yet. Fill in a tool and command, then press Test to see how it would be judged.
en.card.dryRunHint: Judge one call against the rules in force. Runs no tool and writes no rule — check a rule here before you change it.
en.card.dryRunNoRules: (0 rules loaded — check the rulesFile path)
en.card.dryRunNote: "Matched rule" comes from the rule layer. When the verdict was produced by an earlier hard-deny or by the keyword blacklist there is no rule index — the dimensions listed are then informational only.
en.card.extraContentArgKeys: Appended document keys (never read as an operation)
en.card.extraContentArgKeysHint: Document field names beyond the built-in list (content/text/plan…): once listed, their text stops entering the flattened scan that the destructive-word blacklist and the credential pre-screen read. Additive only — the built-in list cannot be replaced, because dropping one of its keys would silently re-create the bug where a plan gets refused for describing work. The executed command and the mutated path are judged on their own terms; this list cannot switch them off.
en.card.extraOperationArgKeys: Appended operation keys (read this field as code that runs)
en.card.extraOperationArgKeysHint: Opens a route for fields whose body really is executed (workflowYaml and friends): their text enters the blacklist and the credential screen, and this list wins when both name the same key. Cost: naming a genuine document field here makes “the plan mentions rm -rf” a refusal reason again.
en.card.healthStale: Host route unavailable (404) — the node half is still an old build; fully restart dsh (not just the browser page) and retry.
en.card.llmKeyHidden: Unset · shown as * after first entry
en.card.llmKeyMasked: Set · type a new value to overwrite
en.card.llmKeyOverwrite: A secret is stored; type a new value and blur to overwrite it.
en.card.llmPreset: Endpoint presets (fills the fields; still editable)
en.card.llmPresetHost: DSH model groups (selecting one switches to the session receiver)
en.card.llmReceiver: llmAssist receiving LLM (OpenAI-compatible; any custom API)
en.card.llmSourceHost: Use the session's current default model (DSH llm service)
en.card.llmSourceHostHint: By default approval grading runs on the model group the DSH session currently uses (the effective value is shown below); leave Provider / Model empty to follow the session, or pick from the dropdown or type to pin one — custom groups you configured in DSH (e.g. local-35b) appear automatically.
en.card.networkEnabledHint: When on, starts a local proxy that intercepts outbound subprocess connections and applies allow/deny rules. Off = zero behavior change.
en.card.networkInjectEnvHint: Writes HTTP(S)_PROXY / ALL_PROXY for subprocesses (and clears NO_PROXY). Off = the listener runs but no process environment is changed.
en.card.networkRebindNote: Takes effect immediately — the proxy rebinds automatically, no plugin reload needed.
en.card.passHint: Runs the deterministic mechanical judge only: an irreversible, unlearnable or unreadable call is blocked and the reason fed back to the main model, everything else runs. No model call, no human prompt — the reviewed form of approval: never, and YOLO with the model taken away.
en.card.permissive: Enable the 自动审查 tier
en.card.permissiveHint: When off, the gate behaves exactly as before.
en.card.riskLearning: riskLearning — verdict learning: neutral-risk asks that the human approves and that execute count up; the same operation auto-allows at threshold with a matching fingerprint
en.card.riskLearningHint: Learning state is plugin-owned ($DSH_HOME/perm-gate/learning.json) and never written into your YAML rules; a different target never reuses authority. Off by default.
en.card.riskSediment: riskSediment — learning sedimentation: threshold-reached samples become deterministic auto-allows
en.card.riskSedimentHint: When on, once a tool|category key reaches the threshold its sample fingerprints are sedimented into allow rules — an exact same-tool same-target hit allows outright without another LLM call (keeps working with llmAssist off).
en.card.rulesFallback: Degrade to a rule-only gate when there is no model (cc-safety-net class)
en.card.rulesFallbackHint: Takes effect only when the risk reviewer is not configured or gave no verdict: the deterministic nets block what they can name and let the rest through, instead of parking the call on a popup nobody will answer. While a reviewer answers, behaviour is unchanged.
en.card.rulesHint: The rules the gate is loading right now (from this plugin entry's `rules` config field; falls back to the rules file when unset). Read-only — nothing here can change them. To change rules, use the allowlist below or edit them on the settings page.
en.card.rulesMissing: Rules not found. The gate falls back to its built-in defaults.
en.card.rulesNote: Read-only: this panel cannot modify the rules. The allowlist section and "allow always" write back to this plugin's entry config.
en.card.rulesTruncated: Rules are large; showing the first 512 KB only.
en.card.scopeNote: Preset scope: this gate only acts while the session permission preset is %scope. Under any other preset the whole gate stands down — P0 hard-deny included — and the selected preset's own policy takes over. A stand-down records one event and leaves a sticky strip above the input.
en.card.scriptReview: Attach script bodies to the review (on by default)
en.card.scriptReviewHint: When a call runs a script file, its body is read and given to the risk model and the human alike, and the deterministic nets grade the body too (a delete that only shows up inside the file is exactly what used to slip through). Bodies are redacted and length-capped before leaving the host; switching this off keeps file contents local at the cost of sending out-of-workspace scripts back to the unreadable tier.
en.card.sedimentEmpty: No sedimented rules yet (samples reaching the threshold appear here)
en.card.sedimentHint: Rules sedimented from human confirmations: only an exact fingerprint hit allows, never a different target. Terminate one learning or remove one sample.
en.card.sedimentStopConfirm: Terminate learning for '%k'? Its count and samples are dropped.
en.card.sedimentStopTitle: Terminate this learning (drops the count and samples)
en.card.strategies: Backend approval strategies (at least one effective; combinable)
en.card.strategy.alwaysConfirm: alwaysConfirm — every crossing asks; the approval "allow controls" get two extended buttons: "repeat-allow this type this session" (bounded session grant) and "allow every occurrence" (persist the command word into the rulesFile whitelist)
en.card.strategy.llmAssist: llmAssist — a custom LLM grades risk: safe auto-allows; deletion/credential/remote/system/bulk hard risks keep the human ask (the classifier never denies — it only escalates); neutral enters confirm-learning; failure/timeout falls back to the human
en.card.strategy.trustAutoAllow: trustAutoAllow — safe in-scope ops auto-allow; dangerous/unknown ask (baseline middle tier)
en.card.strategy.trustEscalation: trustEscalation — sandbox escalation without a prompt: for a call this gate already allowed, the sandbox widening a shell / pwsh / edit tool raises from inside itself is approved here instead of asking you
en.card.strategy.trustEscalationHint: A sandbox escalation is asked from inside the tool body, after tools/pre-execute, so the gate never saw it — a call the LLM graded safe and the gate auto-allowed still prompted you to approve the widening. With this on, only the exact call the gate allowed (matched by callId) skips the prompt; everything else goes to the human as before, as does any unrecognized reason or a target other than workspace-write / danger-full-access. Turn it off to keep widening human-gated.
en.card.tierScopeHint: Only presets inside the gate's scope (%scope) reach this step; outside it the whole gate stands down, so no switch takes over its confirmations.
en.card.title: 自动审查 (Auto review)
en.card.unattended: Unattended tiers (three implementations — each switch decides whether its own tier exists)
en.card.unattendedHint: Three switches, each governing only the tier named beside it: switching an implementation off returns that tier to the ordinary human flow — it never quietly becomes a different tier.
en.card.unavailable: Settings namespace unavailable: make sure dsh-perm-gate is assembled into this profile.
en.card.watchHint: When on, automatically watches rule files for changes and applies them instantly without manual reload.
en.card.yolo: YOLO — never ask a human: block the dangerous, run the rest
en.card.yoloHint: Blocks an irreversible / unlearnable / unreadable payload, or a hard-risk verdict from the model, and feeds the reason back to the main LLM as a 工具审核意见 message; everything else executes. With no reviewer available only the deterministic nets catch anything.
en.doubt.exec-external: it runs code from outside the workspace, which this call cannot inspect
en.doubt.irreversible: a rule says this is irreversible: it cannot be undone once run
en.doubt.model-flagged: the risk model flagged it (it can only escalate, never clear)
en.doubt.never-learn: this answer will not be learned; the same call will ask again next time
en.doubt.no-rule: no rule covers this call, so the default is to ask — that does not mean it is dangerous
en.doubt.opaque: the payload cannot be read (encoded, a script outside the workspace, or no recognisable program), so no rule can locate its target
en.doubt.outside-paths: it touches paths outside the workspace
en.doubt.remote-write: it has an externally visible effect (push / publish / write request); undoing it takes extra manual steps
en.history.clearAllConfirm: Clear diff snapshots for ALL sessions? This may delete change comparisons other sessions have not reviewed yet, and cannot be undone.
en.history.clearAllTitle: Clear diff snapshots for every session, including ones never reviewed — asks again
en.history.clearSessionConfirm: Clear this session’s diff snapshots? Only the change-comparison data produced by this session’s approvals is removed; the approval records stay.
en.history.clearSessionTitle: Clear only this session’s diff snapshots (other sessions untouched)
en.history.diffEmpty: No content change (or the file is unreadable)
en.history.diffNoSnapshot: This event has no snapshot for that file
en.history.diffRevertSent: Revert instruction sent to the conversation; the AI will restore the file accordingly
en.history.empty: No approval records in this session yet
en.history.label: Approvals
en.history.subtitle: Every gate decision in this conversation, newest first
en.history.title: Permission approval records
